title: Hollandaise Sauce
description: One of the five classic French mother sauces, made by emulsifying egg yolks with warm clarified butter and brightened with lemon juice, creating a rich, velvety sauce for eggs, fish, and vegetables.

ingredients.title: For the Hollandaise Sauce
items: Fresh lemon juice (or white wine vinegar reduction) – 1 tbsp
Cayenne pepper or white pepper – a pinch

instruction.title: Step 1 – Preparing the Bain-Marie
steps: Fill a saucepan with a small amount of water and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Place the egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof stainless-steel bowl over the bain-marie, ensuring the bowl does not touch the simmering water.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Whisking the Egg Yolks
steps: Whisk the egg yolk mixture continuously until it becomes pale, thick, and forms ribbons.
Remove the bowl from direct heat once the desired consistency is reached.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Creating the Emulsion
steps: Slowly drizzle in the warm clarified butter while whisking constantly.
Continue whisking until the sauce becomes thick, glossy, and silky with a stable emulsion.

instruction.title: Step 4 – Seasoning & Finishing
steps: Season with salt and a pinch of cayenne pepper or white pepper.
Adjust the acidity with additional lemon juice if desired.
Serve immediately or keep warm over lukewarm water, avoiding excessive heat to prevent the sauce from splitting.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve over Eggs Benedict for a classic brunch dish.
Pair with steamed asparagus, broccoli, or other tender vegetables.
Drizzle over poached or grilled fish.
Use as the base for Béarnaise, Mousseline, or Maltaise sauces.

chefTips: Maintain gentle heat throughout the process to avoid scrambling the egg yolks.
Add the clarified butter slowly to achieve a smooth and stable emulsion.
If the sauce becomes too thick, whisk in a teaspoon of warm water to loosen it.
Serve immediately for the best texture and flavor, as Hollandaise does not reheat well.
Avoid overheating the finished sauce, as excessive heat can cause it to split.
